title: D-FINE-M vs RT-DETR-R50m: same-protocol benchmark
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol: D-FINE-M leads by 4.0 mAP points on half the VRAM, but RT-DETR-R50m is faster on desktop GPU and the order flips on edge.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: D-FINE-M is the more accurate detector: 57.8 vs 53.8 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R50m on an RTX 5070 Ti, a 4.0 point lead, with roughly half the parameters (19.59M vs 36.59M) and less VRAM (189 vs 302 MB). RT-DETR-R50m wins desktop-GPU speed, 35.3 vs 28.8 FPS. On the edge that reverses: on Jetson Orin D-FINE-M runs 7.0 FPS to RT-DETR-R50m's 5.0.

D-FINE-M (19.59M parameters, Apache-2.0) and RT-DETR-R50m (36.59M, Apache-2.0) are both mid-size detectors evaluated at 640 px on COCO val2017. D-FINE-M is the smaller model. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, A100, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5, so this comparison covers the deploy targets where the ranking changes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. D-FINE-M and RT-DETR-R50m highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. D-FINE-M measures 57.8 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R50m's 53.8, and the lead holds across runtimes. The gap is widest on small objects: 43.0 vs 37.6 mAP_small, a 14.24% relative gap. If small instances dominate your scenes, that row decides it.

On the RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, RT-DETR-R50m runs 35.3 FPS to D-FINE-M's 28.8, so it is 18.46% faster. The margin widens under conversion: 76.4 vs 59.8 FPS on ONNX Runtime and 102.8 vs 85.3 FPS on TensorRT FP32.

The speed verdict does not travel to the edge. On Jetson Orin D-FINE-M runs 7.0 FPS to RT-DETR-R50m's 5.0, and on Raspberry Pi 5 it leads 0.6 to 0.4 FPS. If your target is a Jetson or a Pi, the desktop numbers point the wrong way.

Pick D-FINE-M for accuracy, memory, or edge serving: it leads at every object size, uses less VRAM, and is faster on both Jetson Orin and Raspberry Pi 5. Pick RT-DETR-R50m for desktop or server GPU throughput, where it is faster on every GPU runtime measured. Both are Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

dfine  = LibreYOLO("LibreDFINEm.pt")      # 19.59M params, 57.8 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr50m.pt")  # 36.59M params, 53.8 mAP@50-95

results = dfine("image.jpg")
